explanation: A risk ratio of 0.84 (below 1) in a cohort study means that the exposure (drinking green tea) is associated with a lower risk of diabetes. Whether it is statistically significant depends on the confidence interval.

stem: Which statement refers best to the criteria for starting an urban community health center?
options: Caters to a population of 1-1.5 lakh
Referral center for 2-3 primary health centers
No sub-district and district hospitals present in the area
Should have a 100-bed facility in metro cities
explanation: According to the key, an urban community health centre should have a 100-bed facility in metro cities. Other details in the options do not match the criteria.

stem: How is a broken vaccine vial disposed of, according to biomedical waste management?
explanation: Glass vaccine vials (broken or empty) are disposed of in a puncture-proof, leak-proof blue cardboard box or container, as per the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules 2016.

stem: In an urban area in the state of Madhya Pradesh, a primigravida goes for institutional delivery after being motivated by an ASHA worker. What are the benefits they will receive (in terms of money in rupees) under the Janani Suraksha Yojana? ASHA-Accredited social health activist
explanation: Under Janani Suraksha Yojana in low performing states (including Madhya Pradesh), an urban woman gets Rs 1000 and the ASHA Rs 400. In rural areas it is Rs 1400 and Rs 600.

stem: Which of the following agencies provides seed and manure in applied nutrition programs in schools?
explanation: Under the applied nutrition programme (ANP), the key says UNICEF supplies seeds and manure and the Department of Agriculture the technical advice.

stem: Many children from a particular community coming to a hospital were detected to have acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). It was assumed that it is due to the presence of cytotoxic waste in the water of that community. If a case-control study has to be done to find whether the chemical and ALL are associated, what will be taken as the control?
options: Children from the area exposed, but unaffected with the disease
Children from the area not exposed and affected with the disease
Children coming to your OPD, who do not have the disease
All children with ALL irrespective of exposure status
explanation: In a case-control study cases are children with ALL, and controls should be disease-free and come from the same source population, i.e. unaffected children from the same exposed area.

stem: A patient presents with an anesthetic patch in the areas on the face, as shown in the image below. Which of the following nerves is the most commonly involved in this condition?
explanation: An anaesthetic patch on the face in leprosy results from involvement of the cutaneous branches of the facial nerve. The key marks facial nerve. The trigeminal nerve is also commonly involved.

stem: An auxiliary nurse midwife has to conduct a vaccination camp in a village. She received 2 open vials, one of which is a pentavalent vaccine and the other is an MR vaccine. What can she do regarding the utilization of these vials?
options: Use MR vaccine and discard pentavalent vaccine
Use pentavalent vaccine and discard MR vaccine
explanation: Under the open-vial policy, an opened multi-dose vial of liquid pentavalent vaccine can be reused for up to 28 days if kept cold and uncontaminated. Lyophilised vaccines such as MR must be discarded 6 hours after reconstitution or at the end of the session, whichever is earlier.

stem: A female patient with a body mass index of 30 kg/m2 presents to you with a lesion on the neck, as shown below. Which of the following conditions is the most likely to be suffering from?
explanation: Velvety, hyperpigmented thickening of the skin of the neck is acanthosis nigricans, a marker of insulin resistance in obesity, metabolic syndrome and PCOS.

stem: A patient with cervical lymphadenopathy and is found to be retropositive. A fungal culture depicts a velvety growth with red diffusible pigment on the underside, as shown below. Which is the most likely causative organism?
explanation: In an HIV-positive patient, a mould that produces a red diffusible pigment on the reverse side of the colony is Talaromyces (Penicillium) marneffei, a thermally dimorphic fungus found in Southeast Asia.
